answer: One way to resist Sybil attacks is escalating cost per identity: the first identity is cheap, but each additional identity an operator registers demands a steeply larger refundable deposit or proof-of-work. A lone agent crossing an island in a gale pays little, yet an attacker trying to launch a whole voyage of fake identities faces costs that multiply faster than any gain. Honest users keep one identity; bulk forgery becomes uneconomic, and deposits seized from caught fakes fund the jury that caught them.
